main.desc: Frenchman executed for blasphemy and sacrilege

events.text: Joint reading of Charles Darwin and Alfred Russel Wallace's papers on evolution to the Linnean Society of London.

main.t: Princess Alice of the United Kingdom

The United States Department of Justice formally comes into existence.
Prince Edward Island joins into Canadian Confederation.

Canada joins the Universal Postal Union.

main.desc: Specialized agency of the United Nations

events.text: Charles Taze Russell publishes the first edition of the religious magazine The Watchtower.

main.desc: Founder of the Bible Student movement (1852–1916)

The United States terminates reciprocity and fishery agreement with Canada.

main.desc: Term in Canadian politics for free trade with the United States

events.text: The Congo Free State is established by King Leopold II of Belgium.
Canada and Bermuda are linked by telegraph cable.

main.desc: British Overseas Territory in the North Atlantic

events.text: Spanish–American War: The Battle of San Juan Hill is fought in Santiago de Cuba, Cuba.

main.desc: 1898 conflict between Spain and the United States

Start of first Tour de France bicycle race.
SOS is adopted as the international distress signal.

main.desc: International Morse code distress signal for help

events.text: Germany dispatches the gunboat SMS Panther to Morocco, sparking the Agadir Crisis.

main.desc: 1917 – Last Russian offensive of World War I

Yan Ruisheng (advertisement pictured), the first full-length Chinese film, is released in Shanghai.

main.desc: 1921 Chinese silent film by Ren Pengnian

main.desc: Governing party of the People's Republic of China

links.t: Communist Party of the Soviet Union

links.t: History of Chinese immigration to Canada

main.desc: World War I memorial in St. John's, Newfoundland and Labrador

events.text: The Singapore Improvement Trust was founded to oversee the construction of public housing in Singapore, where more than three quarters of residents live.
United Airlines begins service (as Boeing Air Transport).
Wiley Post and Harold Gatty become the first people to circumnavigate the globe in a single-engined monoplane aircraft (a Lockheed Vega).
Australia's national broadcaster, the Australian Broadcasting Corporation, is formed.
The first Grant Park Music Festival was held in Chicago's Grant Park.

main.desc: Classical music concert series in Chicago, Illinois

events.text: In Regina, Saskatchewan, police and Royal Canadian Mounted Police ambush strikers participating in the On-to-Ottawa Trek.
Second World War: The Grand Quartier Général of the French Army was disbanded, following the French surrender.
World War II: start of the First Battle of El Alamein.
The Australian Federal Government becomes the sole collector of income tax in Australia as State Income Tax is abolished.
The City of Tokyo and the Prefecture of Tokyo are both replaced by the Tokyo Metropolis.
Crossroads Able is the first postwar nuclear weapon test.

main.desc: 1946 nuclear weapon tests at Bikini Atoll

events.text: The Philippine Air Force is established.

main.desc: Air warfare branch of the Armed Forces of the Philippines

events.text: The first flight departed New York City's John F. Kennedy International Airport, then known as New York International Airport.

main.desc: International airport serving New York City

events.text: Muhammad Ali Jinnah (Quaid-i-Azam) inaugurates Pakistan's central bank, the State Bank of Pakistan.

The merger of two princely states of India, Cochin and Travancore, into the state of Thiru-Kochi (later re-organized as Kerala) in the Indian Union ends more than 1,000 years of princely rule by the Cochin royal family.
The International Geophysical Year begins.
The Canadian Broadcasting Corporation links television broadcasting across Canada via microwave.
Flooding of Canada's Saint Lawrence Seaway begins.

main.desc: System of waterways in Canada and the US

Ghana became a republic, with Kwame Nkrumah as its first president.

The Trust Territory of Somaliland (the former Italian Somaliland) gains its independence from Italy. Concurrently, it unites as scheduled with the five-day-old State of Somaliland (the former British Somaliland) to form the Somali Republic.
Ghana becomes a republic and Kwame Nkrumah becomes its first President as Queen Elizabeth II ceases to be its head of state.
Independence of Rwanda and Burundi.
ZIP codes are introduced for United States mail.

The People's Liberation Army Rocket Force (first known as the 2nd Artillery Corps) is founded.

main.desc: 1965 unification of the three economic communities of Europe

events.text: The United States Central Intelligence Agency's Phoenix Program is officially established.

main.desc: U.S. intelligence and covert action agency

main.t: Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons

events.text: Formal separation of the United Auto Workers from the AFL–CIO in the United States.
The Belfast Banking Company, which issued banknotes in Northern Ireland, merged with its rival Northern Bank.
The first Gay pride march in England takes place.
Portugal grants autonomy to Madeira.

main.desc: Portuguese archipelago in the North Atlantic

events.text: The Northern Territory in Australia is granted self-government.

Sony introduces the Walkman.

The PG-13 rating is introduced by the MPAA.

main.desc: Clear-channel sports radio station in New York City

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

Croatia becomes the 28th member of the European Union.

main.desc: Country in Central and Southeast Europe

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1740 to 1758

Anne Frank and her family go into hiding in the "Secret Annexe" above her father's office in an Amsterdam warehouse.
Jackie Robinson refuses to move to the back of a bus, leading to his court-martial.

main.desc: 1944 mass fatality fire disaster in Hartford, Connecticut

The AK-47 goes into production in the Soviet Union.
Althea Gibson wins at the Wimbledon Championships, becoming the first black athlete to do so.

main.desc: U.S. program examining the peaceful applications of nuclear explosives (1961–1977)

main.t: The Late Late Show (Irish talk show)

The Comoros declares independence from France.

main.desc: African island country in the Indian Ocean

main.desc: 2013 Boko Haram attack in Mamudo, Nigeria

Battle of Vítkov Hill, decisive victory of Czech Hussite forces commanded by Jan Žižka against Crusade army led by Sigismund, Holy Roman Emperor.
Joan of Arc, taken by the Burgundians in May, is handed over to Pierre Cauchon, the bishop of Beauvais.
1454–1466 Thirteen Years' War: The Battle for Kneiphof ended with a decisive victory for the Teutonic Order.

main.desc: Conflict between the Prussian Confederation, Poland, and the Teutonic Order

events.text: John Hunyadi and his forces defeat the Ottoman fleet on the Danube, allowing them to reinforce and supply the besieged city of Belgrade.
Anglo-Spanish War: English and Dutch troops sack the Spanish city of Cádiz before leaving the next day.

main.desc: War between the kingdoms of Spain and England

events.text: An expedition led by Gaspar de Portolá leaves its base in San Diego and sets out to find the Port of Monterey (now Monterey, California).

main.desc: Exploration of the present-day state of California, United States, 1769–1770

events.text: Foundation of the Mission San Antonio de Padua in modern California by the Franciscan friar Junípero Serra.
The Bastille, a fortress and prison in Paris, was stormed by a crowd during the flashpoint of the French Revolution.
Storming of the Bastille in Paris. This event escalates the widespread discontent into the French Revolution. Bastille Day is still celebrated annually in France.

main.desc: Major event of the French Revolution

events.text: Inaugural Fête de la Fédération is held to celebrate the unity of the French people and the national reconciliation.
The Priestley Riots, targeting religious dissenters such as Joseph Priestley, began in Birmingham, England.
Beginning of Priestley Riots (to 17 July) in Birmingham targeting Joseph Priestley as a supporter of the French Revolution.
The Sedition Act became law, making it a federal crime to write, publish, or utter false or malicious statements about the U.S. federal government.

main.desc: Set of 1798 laws in the United States

links.t: Federal government of the United States

events.text: The Sedition Act of 1798 becomes law in the United States making it a federal crime to write, publish, or utter false or malicious statements about the United States government.

main.desc: Set of 1798 laws in the United States

links.t: Federal crime in the United States

events.text: The Finnish War: the Battle of Lapua is fought.
Opening of the first major US world's fair, the Exhibition of the Industry of All Nations in New York City.

links.t: Exhibition of the Industry of All Nations

events.text: A seven-man mountaineering team made the first ascent of the Matterhorn, marking the end of the golden age of alpinism.
The first ascent of the Matterhorn is completed by Edward Whymper and his party, four of whom die on the descent.
A fire destroyed 812 structures and killed 20 people in Chicago, leading to reforms in the city's fire-prevention and firefighting efforts.
The Chicago Fire of 1874 burns down 47 acres of the city, destroying 812 buildings, killing 20, and resulting in the fire insurance industry demanding municipal reforms from Chicago's city council.
While on the run from a death sentence, American outlaw Billy the Kid was shot and killed by Sherriff Pat Garrett in Fort Sumner, New Mexico.
American outlaw Billy the Kid is shot and killed by Sheriff Pat Garrett in the Maxwell House at Fort Sumner, New Mexico.
Armies of the Eight-Nation Alliance capture Tientsin during the Boxer Rebellion.
The medieval St Mark's Campanile in Venice collapsed, also demolishing the Loggetta del Sansovino.

main.desc: Basilica bell tower in Venice, Italy

events.text: An expedition led by Peruvian explorer and farmer Agustín Lizárraga discovered the Incan city of Machu Picchu (pictured).
Peruvian explorer and farmer Agustín Lizárraga discovers Machu Picchu, the "Lost City of the Incas".
The Campanile in St Mark's Square, Venice collapses, also demolishing the loggetta.

main.desc: Basilica bell tower in Venice, Italy

events.text: Harry Atwood, an exhibition pilot for the Wright brothers, is greeted by president William Howard Taft after he lands his aeroplane on the South Lawn of the White House, having flown from Boston.

main.desc: American inventor, engineer, and aviation pioneer (1883–1967)

events.text: Beginning of the McMahon–Hussein Correspondence between Hussein bin Ali, Sharif of Mecca and the British official Henry McMahon concerning the Arab Revolt against the Ottoman Empire.

main.desc: 1915–16 letters on UK recognition of Arab independence

events.text: The Battle of Delville Wood began as an action within the Battle of the Somme, lasting until 3 September 1916.
World War I:   Battle of Delville Wood begins as an action within the Battle of the Somme, lasting until 3 September 1916.
In a decree called the Gleichschaltung, Adolf Hitler abolishes all German political parties except the Nazis.

Nazi eugenics programme begins with the proclamation of the Law for the Prevention of Hereditarily Diseased Offspring requiring the compulsory sterilization of any citizen who suffers from alleged genetic disorders.

main.desc: Nazi German policy of the murder of "undesirable" persons

links.t: Law for the Prevention of Hereditarily Diseased Offspring

events.text: In the Wardha session of Congress, the "Quit India" resolution is approved, authorising Mahatma Gandhi to campaign for India's independence from Britain.
In Diamond, Missouri, the George Washington Carver National Monument becomes the first United States National Monument in honor of an African American.
Palmiro Togliatti, leader of the Italian Communist Party, is shot and wounded near the Italian Parliament.
Korean War: North Korean troops began attacking the headquarters of the American 24th Infantry Division in present-day Daejeon, South Korea.
Korean War: beginning of the Battle of Taejon.
Ferrari take their first Formula One grand prix victory at the British Grand Prix at Silverstone.
Rawya Ateya takes her seat in the National Assembly of Egypt, thereby becoming the first female parliamentarian in the Arab world.
In the 14 July Revolution in Iraq, the monarchy is overthrown by popular forces led by Abd al-Karim Qasim, who becomes the nation's new leader.
Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 1-11 ditched off Polillo Island in the Philippines, killing one person and injuring 44 others.
Jane Goodall arrives at the Gombe Stream Reserve in present-day Tanzania to begin her study of chimpanzees in the wild.
Northwest Orient Airlines Flight 1-11 ditches off Polillo Island in the Philippines, killing one person and injuring 44.
Mariner 4 flyby of Mars takes the first close-up photos of another planet. The photographs take approximately six hours to be transmitted back to Earth.

main.desc: First successful NASA mission to Mars (1964–1967)

events.text: Mario Bros. is released in Japan, beginning the popular Super Mario Bros franchise.
More than 100 mm (3.9 in) of rain fell in a two-and-a-half-hour period in parts of Montreal, causing severe flooding.
Australian criminal Bradley John Murdoch murders British tourist Peter Falconio and abducts his girlfriend in the Northern Territory.
Rus Flight 9633 crashes during takeoff from Chkalovsky Airport, killing all 10 people on board.
French president Jacques Chirac escapes an assassination attempt from Maxime Brunerie during a Bastille Day parade at Champs-Élysées.
Valerie Plame's identity as a CIA operative was leaked to and published by journalist Robert Novak.

main.desc: American writer, spy novelist and former CIA officer (born 1963)

events.text: Dedication of the statue of Rachel Carson, a sculpture of the environmentalist, in Woods Hole, Massachusetts.

main.desc: Monument in Woods Hole, Massachusetts, United States

events.text: Lightning strikes started four fires in the Methow Valley in the U.S. state of Washington, collectively known as the Carlton Complex Fire.
NASA's New Horizons probe performs the first flyby of Pluto, and thus completes the initial survey of the Solar System.
A man deliberately drove a truck into crowds in Nice, France, resulting in 86 deaths.
A man ploughs a truck into a Bastille Day celebration in Nice, France, killing 86 people and injuring another 434 before being shot by police.
A GippsAero GA8 Airvan crashes in Umeå, Sweden, killing all nine aboard.
Dedication of the Temple of Castor and Pollux in ancient Rome.

main.desc: Ancient temple in the Roman Forum in Rome, Italy

events.text: First Jewish–Roman War: Titus and his armies breach the walls of Jerusalem. (17th of Tammuz in the Hebrew calendar).

An Lushan Rebellion: Emperor Xuanzong of Tang is ordered by his Imperial Guards to execute chancellor Yang Guozhong by forcing him to commit suicide or face a mutiny. General An Lushan has other members of the emperor's family killed.

main.desc: 755–763 uprising against Tang rule in China

events.text: First Crusade: Christian soldiers take the Church of the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem after the final assault of a difficult siege.

main.desc: 1096–1099 Christian re-conquest of the Holy Land

events.text: The reconstructed Church of the Holy Sepulchre is consecrated in Jerusalem.
King John of England expels Canterbury monks for supporting Archbishop Stephen Langton.
Swedish–Novgorodian Wars: A Novgorodian army led by Alexander Nevsky defeats the Swedes in the Battle of the Neva.
John Ball, a leader in the Peasants' Revolt, is hanged, drawn and quartered in the presence of King Richard II of England.
The Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeated the Teutonic Knights at the Battle of Grunwald, the decisive engagement of the Polish–Lithuanian–Teutonic War.

main.t: Crown of the Kingdom of Poland
main.desc: 1385–1795 territorial possessions of the King of Poland

events.text: Polish–Lithuanian–Teutonic War: Battle of Grunwald: The allied forces of the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania defeat the army of the Teutonic Order.

links.t: History of Poland during the Jagiellonian dynasty

events.text: Muhammad XI is crowned the twenty-second and last Nasrid king of Granada.

main.desc: Ruler of the Emirate of Grenada (1460–1533)

events.text: The first university of Finland, the Royal Academy of Turku, is inaugurated in Turku.

main.desc: University in Finland (1640 to 1828); now the University of Helsinki

events.text: Baruch Laibov and Alexander Voznitsyn are burned alive in St. Petersburg, Russia. Vonitzin had converted to Judaism with Laibov's help, with the consent of Empress Anna Ivanovna.
Aleksei Chirikov sights land in Southeast Alaska. He sends men ashore in a longboat, making them the first Europeans to visit Alaska.
French Revolution: Gilbert du Motier, Marquis de Lafayette, is named by acclamation Colonel General of the new National Guard of Paris.
French soldiers at Fort Julien, near the Egyptian port city of Rashid, uncovered the Rosetta Stone, which was essential in the decipherment of ancient Egyptian scripts.

main.desc: Fort in Egypt on the Nile

events.text: The Rosetta Stone is found in the Egyptian village of Rosetta by French Captain Pierre-François Bouchard during Napoleon's Egyptian Campaign.

main.desc: Egyptian stele with three versions of a 196 BC decree

events.text: Pike Expedition: United States Army Lieutenant Zebulon Pike begins an expedition from Fort Bellefontaine near St. Louis, Missouri,  to explore the west.

main.desc: 1806–07 U.S. exploration of the southwest Louisiana Territory

events.text: Aboard HMS Bellerophon, French emperor Napoleon surrendered to Royal Navy captain Frederick Lewis Maitland, concluding the Napoleonic Wars.

main.desc: Third-rate ship of the line of the Royal Navy

events.text: Napoleonic Wars: Napoleon Bonaparte surrenders aboard HMS Bellerophon.

main.desc: 1803–1815 series of wars led by Napoleon

events.text: A fire destroys the ancient Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls in Rome, Italy.

main.t: Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls
main.desc: Roman Catholic basilica and landmark in Rome, Italy

events.text: The Spanish Inquisition is officially disbanded after nearly 356 years.

main.desc: System of tribunals enforcing Catholic doctrine

events.text: Ralph Waldo Emerson delivers the Divinity School Address at Harvard Divinity School, discounting Biblical miracles and declaring Jesus a great man, but not God. The Protestant community reacts with outrage.
The Great Powers of Europe conclude the convention of London in order to stabilise the Near East.
The first air raid in history occurs; Austria launches pilotless balloons against the city of Venice.

American Civil War: The CSS Arkansas, the most effective ironclad on the Mississippi River, battles with Union Navy ships commanded by Admiral David Farragut, severely damaging three ships and sustaining heavy damage herself.
Following the transfer of Rupert's Land from the Hudson's Bay Company, Manitoba was established as a province of Canada.
Reconstruction Era of the United States: Georgia becomes the last of the former Confederate states to be readmitted to the Union.

Canadian Confederation: Rupert's Land and the North-Western Territory are transferred to Canada from the Hudson's Bay Company, and the province of Manitoba and the Northwest Territories are established from these vast territories.
The stratovolcano Mount Bandai erupts, killing approximately 500 people in Fukushima Prefecture, Japan.

main.desc: Type of conical volcano composed of layers of lava and tephra

events.text: In his book Clinical Psychiatry, Emil Kraepelin gives a name to Alzheimer's disease, naming it after his colleague Alois Alzheimer.
In Seattle, Washington, William Boeing and George Conrad Westervelt incorporate Pacific Aero Products (later renamed Boeing).
World War I: The Second Battle of the Marne begins near the River Marne with a German attack.
Aftermath of World War I: The Parliament of Poland establishes Silesian Voivodeship before the Polish-German plebiscite.

main.desc: Events after the end of the war in 1918

events.text: The Japanese Communist Party is established in Japan.
Massacre of July 15, 1927: Eighty-nine protesters are killed by Austrian police in Vienna.

main.desc: Riots in Vienna, First Austrian Republic

events.text: The Holocaust: Nazi Germany begins the deportation of 100,000 Jews from the occupied Netherlands to extermination camps.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: The all-female Emilia Plater Independent Women's Battalion was formed in the Soviet Union's First Polish Army.
The State of North Borneo, now Sabah, Malaysia, is annexed by the United Kingdom.

main.desc: British protectorate in Asia from 1877 to 1946

events.text: The Boeing 367-80, the prototype for both the Boeing 707 and C-135 series, takes its first flight.
Eighteen Nobel laureates sign the Mainau Declaration against nuclear weapons, later co-signed by thirty-four others.

main.desc: Prizes established by Alfred Nobel in 1895

events.text: Vietnam War: The United States and South Vietnam begin Operation Hastings to push the North Vietnamese out of the Vietnamese Demilitarized Zone.
The United Red Army is founded in Japan.
In Nicosia, Cyprus, Greek junta-sponsored nationalists launch a coup d'état, deposing Makarios III and installing Nikos Sampson as the president of Cyprus.

main.desc: Capital of the Republic of Cyprus

events.text: Space Race: Apollo–Soyuz Test Project features the dual launch of an Apollo spacecraft and a Soyuz spacecraft on the first Soviet-United States human-crewed flight. It was the last launch of both an Apollo spacecraft, and the Saturn family of rockets.
U.S. president Jimmy Carter gives his "malaise speech".
Sega's first home video game console, the SG-1000 (pictured), was released in Japan.
An attack at Orly Airport in Paris is launched by Armenian militant organisation ASALA, leaving eight people dead and 55 injured.

main.desc: Bombing in Orly airport by ASALA

links.t: Armenian Secret Army for the Liberation of Armenia

events.text: Nintendo and Sega enter the console market with the respective releases of the Famicom and SG-1000 in Japan.
A Belgian Air Force C-130 Hercules carrying the Royal Netherlands Army marching band crashes on landing at Eindhoven Airport.

main.desc: Aviation branch of Belgian Armed Forces

events.text: Sri Lankan Civil War: Sri Lankan Tamil MP S. Shanmuganathan is killed by a claymore mine.
"American Taliban" John Walker Lindh pleads guilty to supplying aid to the enemy and possession of explosives during the commission of a felony.
The Anti-Terrorism Court of Pakistan sentences British-born Ahmed Omar Saeed Sheikh to death, and three others suspected of murdering The Wall Street Journal reporter Daniel Pearl to life.

main.desc: Court dealing with cases of terrorism in Pakistan

events.text: AOL Time Warner disbands Netscape. The Mozilla Foundation is established on the same day.
Twitter, later one of the largest social media platforms in the world, is launched.
Caspian Airlines Flight 7908 crashed in northwestern Iran, killing all 168 people aboard.

A .mw-parser-output .tooltip-dotted{border-bottom:1px dotted;cursor:help}Mw 7.8 earthquake struck a remote region of Fiordland, New Zealand, the country's largest earthquake magnitude since the 1931 Hawke's Bay earthquake.
Caspian Airlines Flight 7908 crashes near Jannatabad, Qazvin, Iran, killing 168.
Space Shuttle program: Endeavour is launched on STS-127 to complete assembly of the International Space Station's Kibō module.
South Korean rapper Psy (pictured) released his hit single "Gangnam Style".
South Korean rapper Psy releases his hit single Gangnam Style.
A train derails on the Moscow Metro, killing at least 24 and injuring more than 160 others.
The Peace at Home Council, a faction of the Turkish Armed Forces, staged a coup d'état attempt against the government and President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan.

main.desc: Executive body that led the 2016 Turkish coup d'état attempt

events.text: Factions of the Turkish Armed Forces attempt a coup.
Croatian Mario Mandžukić scored the first own goal in a FIFA World Cup final in their defeat to France.
France win their second World Cup title, defeating Croatia 4–2.
The Hijrah of Muhammad begins, marking the beginning of the Islamic calendar.

main.desc: Journey of Muhammad from Mecca to Medina

events.text: Battle of Spercheios: Bulgarian forces of Tsar Samuel are defeated by a Byzantine army under general Nikephoros Ouranos at the Spercheios River in Greece.

Three Roman legates place - acting illegally on their own authority - a bull of excommunication against Michael I Cerularius, the patriarch of Constantinople, and his followers on the altar of Hagia Sophia during Saturday afternoon divine liturgy. Historians frequently describe the event as the formal start of the East–West Schism.

Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa: After Pope Innocent III calls European knights to a crusade, the forces of kings Alfonso VIII of Castile, Sancho VII of Navarre, Peter II of Aragon and Afonso II of Portugal defeat those of the Berber Muslim leader Almohad, thus marking a significant turning point in the Reconquista and in the medieval history of Spain.

main.t: Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa
main.desc: Part of the Reconquista in Spain (1212)

events.text: Muhammad ibn Yusuf, who later established the Emirate of Granada, the last Muslim state in Spain, was elected the ruler of Arjona.

main.desc: First ruler of the Emirate of Granada from c. 1232 to 1273

events.text: The Spanish town of Arjona declares independence and names its native Muhammad ibn Yusuf as ruler. This marks the Muhammad's first rise to prominence; he later established the Nasrid Emirate of Granada, the last independent Muslim state in Spain.
Celebrated by the Carmelite Order–but doubted by modern historians–as the day when Saint Simon Stock had a vision of the Virgin Mary.
The ten-year-old Richard II was crowned King of England at Westminster Abbey.
King Richard II of England is crowned.
Jacques Cartier, navigator and explorer, returns home to St. Malo after claiming Stadacona (Quebec), Hochelaga (Montreal) and the River of Canada (St. Lawrence River) region for France.

main.desc: French maritime explorer of North America (1491–1557)

events.text: The first banknotes in Europe are issued by the Swedish bank Stockholms Banco.

main.desc: Paper money issued by a bank

events.text: Manchu Qing dynasty naval forces under commander Shi Lang defeat the Kingdom of Tungning in the Battle of Penghu near the Pescadores Islands.
Father Junípero Serra founds California's first mission, Mission San Diego de Alcalá. Over the following decades, it evolves into the city of San Diego, California.
American Revolutionary War: Light infantry of the Continental Army seize a fortified British Army position in a midnight bayonet attack at the Battle of Stony Point.
Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's opera Die Entführung aus dem Serail premiered in Vienna, after which Emperor Joseph II anecdotally remarked that it had "too many notes".
President George Washington signed the Residence Act, selecting a new permanent site along the Potomac River for the capital of the United States, which later became Washington, D.C.

main.desc: Founding Father, U.S. president from 1789 to 1797

events.text: The District of Columbia is established as the capital of the United States after signature of the Residence Act.

main.desc: Federal capital district of the United States

events.text: The city of La Paz, in what is today Bolivia, declares its independence from the Spanish Crown during the La Paz revolution and forms the Junta Tuitiva, the first independent government in Spanish America, led by Pedro Domingo Murillo.
Antonio María Claret y Clará founds the Congregation of the Missionary Sons of the Immaculate Heart of Mary, popularly known as the Claretians in Vic, in the province of Barcelona, Catalonia, Spain.
The last apparition of the Blessed Virgin Mary to Bernadette Soubirous in Lourdes, France.

main.desc: 1858 reported supernatural activity in Lourdes, France

events.text: American Civil War: At the order of President Abraham Lincoln, Union troops begin a 25-mile march into Virginia for what will become the First Battle of Bull Run, the first major land battle of the war.
American Civil War: David Farragut is promoted to rear admiral, becoming the first officer in United States Navy to hold an admiral rank.
The Imperial Russian army under Grand Duke Nicholas defeats the Ottoman army and takes the city of Nikopol (modern Bulgaria).

links.t: Grand Duke Nicholas Nikolaevich of Russia (born 1831)

events.text: Persian Constitutional Revolution: Mohammad Ali Shah Qajar is forced out as Shah of Persia and is replaced by his son Ahmad Shah Qajar.
John Robertson Duigan makes the first flight of the Duigan pusher biplane, the first aircraft built in Australia.
Henry James becomes a British citizen to highlight his commitment to Britain during the first World War.

At Treasure Island on the Delaware River in the United States, the First Order of the Arrow ceremony takes place and the Order of the Arrow is founded to honor American Boy Scouts who best exemplify the Scout Oath and Law.

main.desc: Major river on the East Coast of the United States

events.text: Max Reger's Hebbel Requiem was first performed in a memorial concert for the composer, conducted by Philipp Wolfrum.

main.desc: German composer, musician, conductor, and teacher (1873–1916)

events.text: Max Reger's Hebbel Requiem is first performed in a memorial concert for the composer, conducted by Philipp Wolfrum.

main.desc: German composer, musician, conductor, and teacher (1873–1916)

events.text: Augusto César Sandino leads a raid on U.S. Marines and Nicaraguan Guardia Nacional that had been sent to apprehend him in the village of Ocotal, but is repulsed by one of the first dive-bombing attacks in history.
Ethiopian emperor Haile Selassie  promulgated the nation's first modern constitution.
Emperor Haile Selassie signs the first constitution of Ethiopia.

main.desc: Title of the ruling monarch of Ethiopia from 1270 to 1974/1975

events.text: The world's first parking meter is installed in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma.

main.desc: Device for collecting money to use a given parking space

events.text: Holocaust: Vel' d'Hiv Roundup (Rafle du Vel' d'Hiv): The government of Vichy France orders the mass arrest of 13,152 Jews who are held at the Vélodrome d'Hiver in Paris before deportation to Auschwitz.

main.desc: Genocide of European Jews by Nazi Germany

events.text: The United States conducted the first detonation of a nuclear weapon during the Trinity test (pictured).
Manhattan Project: The Atomic Age begins when the United States successfully detonates a plutonium-based test nuclear weapon near Alamogordo, New Mexico.

main.desc: World War II Allied nuclear weapons program

events.text: Following token resistance, the city of Nazareth, revered by Christians as the hometown of Jesus, capitulates to Israeli troops during Operation Dekel in the 1948 Arab–Israeli War.

main.desc: Largest city in the Northern District of Israel

events.text: The storming of the cockpit of the Miss Macao passenger seaplane, operated by a subsidiary of the Cathay Pacific Airways, marks the first aircraft hijacking of a commercial plane.

main.desc: Hong Kong commercial seaplane; hijacked by pirates in 1948

events.text: Korean War: A Korean People's Army unit massacred 31 prisoners of war of the U.S. Army on a mountain near the village of Tuman.
Uruguay won the decisive match of the fourth FIFA World Cup, defeating Brazil 2–1 at the Maracanã Stadium in Rio de Janeiro.

links.t: Uruguay v Brazil (1950 FIFA World Cup)

events.text: Chaplain–Medic massacre: American POWs are massacred by North Korean Army.

main.desc: 1950 war crime during the Korean War

events.text: Uruguay beats hosts Brazil 2–1 to win the World Cup in a match dubbed as the Maracanazo.

links.t: Uruguay v Brazil (1950 FIFA World Cup)

events.text: The Catcher in the Rye (cover pictured), an American coming-of-age novel by J. D. Salinger, was published by Little, Brown.

main.desc: 1951 American novel by J. D. Salinger

events.text: King Leopold III of Belgium abdicates in favor of his son, Baudouin of Belgium.

main.desc: King of the Belgians from 1934 to 1951

events.text: J. D. Salinger publishes his popular yet controversial novel, The Catcher in the Rye.
KLM Flight 844 crashes off the Schouten Islands in present day Indonesia (then Netherlands New Guinea), killing 58 people.

South Vietnamese Colonel Phạm Ngọc Thảo (pictured)—an undetected communist spy—was reported dead due to injuries sustained during his capture, but it is generally assumed he was killed on the orders of military officials.

main.t: Army of the Republic of Vietnam

events.text: The Mont Blanc Tunnel linking France and Italy opens.

main.desc: Highway tunnel underneath the Alps connecting France and Italy

events.text: South Vietnamese Colonel Phạm Ngọc Thảo, a formerly undetected communist spy and double agent, is hunted down and killed by unknown individuals after being sentenced to death in absentia for a February 1965 coup attempt against Nguyễn Khánh.

main.t: Army of the Republic of Vietnam

events.text: The Apollo 11 lunar landing mission is launched from Cape Kennedy in Florida, USA.
Iraqi President Ahmed Hassan al-Bakr resigns and is replaced by Saddam Hussein.
A Sikorsky S-61 helicopter operated by British Airways crashed in thick fog in the Celtic Sea, killing 20 of the 26 people on board.
Sikorsky S-61 disaster: A helicopter crashes off the Isles of Scilly, causing 20 fatalities.

main.desc: Accident in the southern Celtic Sea

events.text: A 7.8 MS earthquake struck the densely populated Philippine island of Luzon, killing an estimated 1,621 people.
The Luzon earthquake strikes the Philippines with an intensity of 7.7, affecting Benguet, Pangasinan, Nueva Ecija, La Union, Aurora, Bataan, Zambales and Tarlac.
The Parliament of the Ukrainian SSR declares state sovereignty over the territory of the Ukrainian SSR.

links.t: Declaration of State Sovereignty of Ukraine

events.text: Fragments of Comet Shoemaker–Levy 9 began colliding with the planet Jupiter , with the first impact causing a fireball that reached a peak temperature of 24,000 kelvin.
The comet Shoemaker-Levy 9 is destroyed in a head-on collision with Jupiter.
A faction of the armed forces of São Tomé and Príncipe led by Major Fernando Pereira overthrew the government of Fradique de Menezes in a bloodless coup d'état.

main.t: Armed Forces of São Tomé and Príncipe
main.desc: Combined military forces of São Tomé and Príncipe

links.t: 2003 São Tomé and Príncipe coup d'état

events.text: Millennium Park, a public park in Chicago, Illinois, and one of the world's largest rooftop gardens, opened to the public.

main.desc: Public park in Chicago, Illinois, US

events.text: An Antonov An-24 crashes near Baney in Bioko Norte, Equatorial Guinea, killing 60 people.
A magnitude-6.6 earthquake struck off the coast of Niigata Prefecture, Japan, causing a leak of radioactive gases from the Kashiwazaki-Kariwa Nuclear Power Plant.
An earthquake of magnitude 6.8 and 6.6 aftershock occurs off the Niigata coast of Japan killing eight people, injuring at least 800 and damaging a nuclear power plant.
A tainted milk powder scandal broke in China which ultimately involved an estimated 300,000 victims, the vast majority infants, with 54,000 hospitalized with kidney problems and six deaths.

Teoh Beng Hock, an aide to a politician in Malaysia is found dead on the rooftop of a building adjacent to the offices of the Anti-Corruption Commission, sparking an inquest that gains nationwide attention.
At least 23 students died and dozens more fell ill at a primary school in the Indian state of Bihar after consuming a Midday Meal that was contaminated with pesticide.
As many as 27 children die and 25 others are hospitalized after eating lunch served at their school in eastern India.
Syrian civil war: The Battle of Ras al-Ayn resumes between the People's Protection Units (YPG) and Islamist forces, beginning the Rojava–Islamist conflict.
Four U.S. Marines and a United States Navy Sailor are killed in the a shooting spree targeting military installations in Chattanooga, Tennessee.

main.desc: Naval infantry branch of the U.S. military

events.text: A 100-year-old building in Mumbai, India, collapses, killing at least 10 people and leaving many others trapped.
Twelve inhabitants of Scillium (near Kasserine, modern-day Tunisia) in North Africa are executed for being Christians. This is the earliest record of Christianity in that part of the world.

links.t: Christianity in the Roman Africa province

events.text: Consecration of Pope John III following the death of Pope Pelagius I earlier that year.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 561 to 574

events.text: Damasus II is elected pope, and dies 23 days later.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church in 1048

events.text: Four year-old Henry IV is crowned as king of Germany in Aachen.
The Fourth Crusade assaults Constantinople. The Byzantine emperor Alexios III Angelos flees from his capital into exile.
Zhu Di, better known by his era name as the Yongle Emperor, assumes the throne over the Ming dynasty of China.

main.desc: Name chosen by a reigning monarch, different from their original secular name

events.text: Hundred Years' War: Charles VII of France is crowned the King of France in the Reims Cathedral after a successful campaign by Joan of Arc.
The Battle of Castillon, the last engagement of the Hundred Years' War, ended with the English losing all holdings in France except the Pale of Calais.
Battle of Castillon: The last battle of the Hundred Years' War, the French under Jean Bureau defeat the English under the Earl of Shrewsbury, who is killed in the battle in Gascony.
Sikandar Lodi succeeds Bahlul Khan Lodi as Sultan of Delhi.
King George I of Great Britain sails down the River Thames with a barge of 50 musicians, where George Frideric Handel's Water Music is premiered.

main.desc: King of Great Britain and Ireland from 1714 to 1727

events.text: Former emperor Peter III of Russia is murdered.
Dene men who were acting as guides to Samuel Hearne on his exploration of the Coppermine River in present-day Nunavut, Canada, massacred a group of about twenty Copper Inuit.
Bloody Falls massacre: Chipewyan chief Matonabbee, traveling as the guide to Samuel Hearne on his Arctic overland journey, massacres a group of unsuspecting Inuit.

Members of the French National Guard under the command of General Lafayette open fire on a crowd of radical Jacobins at the Champ de Mars, Paris, during the French Revolution, killing scores of people.

main.desc: French military and police reserve force

events.text: The 16 Carmelite Martyrs of Compiègne are executed ten days prior to the end of the French Revolution's Reign of Terror.
The Kingdom of Spain cedes the territory of Florida to the United States.

main.desc: Country in Southern and Western Europe

events.text: William Cranch Bond and John Adams Whipple took a daguerreotype of Vega, the first astrophotograph of a star other than the Sun.
Vega becomes the first star (other than the Sun) to be photographed.

main.desc: Brightest star in the constellation Lyra

events.text: The garrotting and robbery of James Pilkington, a British member of Parliament, led to a moral panic in London.
The New Zealand Wars resumed as British forces led by General Duncan Cameron began the invasion of the Waikato.
Harvard School of Dental Medicine is established in Boston, Massachusetts. It is the first dental school in the U.S. that is affiliated with a university.

main.desc: Dental school in Boston, Massachusetts, US

events.text: NEC Corporation is organized as the first Japanese joint venture with foreign capital.
RMS Carpathia, which had rescued survivors of the 1912 Titanic sinking, was sunk by a German U-boat with the loss of five crew.

main.desc: Ocean liner known for rescuing survivors of RMS Titanic

events.text: Russian Revolution: Tsar Nicholas II and his family (pictured) were murdered by Bolsheviks at Yekaterinburg.

main.desc: 1917–1922 civil war in the Russian Empire

events.text: Tsar Nicholas II of Russia and his immediate family and retainers are executed by Bolshevik Chekists at the Ipatiev House in Yekaterinburg, Russia.
The RMS Carpathia is sunk off Ireland by the German SM U-55; five lives are lost.

main.desc: Ocean liner known for rescuing survivors of RMS Titanic

events.text: The form of government in the Republic of Finland is officially confirmed with the enactment of the Constitution of Finland. For this reason, July 17 is known as the Day of Democracy (Kansanvallan päivä) in Finland.
Altona Bloody Sunday: A riot between the Nazi Party paramilitary forces, the SS and SA, and the German Communist Party ensues.

main.desc: 1932 clash between Nazi and Communist demonstrators in Prussia

events.text: Nationalist military officers launch a coup d'état against the Spanish Republic, beginning the Spanish Civil War

main.desc: Major faction in the Spanish Civil War of 1936 to 1939

events.text: Spanish Civil War: An Armed Forces rebellion against the recently elected leftist Popular Front government of Spain starts the civil war.
Douglas Corrigan takes off from Brooklyn to fly the "wrong way" to Ireland and becomes known as "Wrong Way" Corrigan.
Laden with munitions for World War II, two ships exploded at the Port Chicago Naval Magazine in California, killing 320 people and injuring more than 400 others.

links.t: Port Chicago Naval Magazine National Memorial

events.text: Port Chicago disaster: Near the San Francisco Bay, two ships laden with ammunition for the war explode in Port Chicago, California, killing 320.

World War II: The main three leaders of the Allied nations, Winston Churchill, Harry S. Truman and Joseph Stalin, hold the Potsdam Conference in the German city of Potsdam to decide the future of a defeated Germany.
In Olympia, Greece, the Summer Olympics torch relay, nicknamed the "relay of peace", began.
The largest number of United States midshipman casualties in a single event results from an aircraft crash in Florida, killing 44.
First Indochina War: Viet Minh troops successfully ambush the armoured French column 'G.M. 42' in the Battle of Chu Dreh Pass in the Central Highlands. It is the last battle of the war.
Nuclear weapons testing: The "Small Boy" test shot Little Feller I becomes the last atmospheric test detonation at the Nevada National Security Site.

main.desc: Controlled detonation of nuclear weapons for scientific or political purposes

events.text: Led by Ahmed Hassan al-Bakr (pictured), the Arab Socialist Ba'ath Party overthrew Iraqi president Abdul Rahman Arif in a bloodless coup.
Abdul Rahman Arif is overthrown and the Ba'ath Party is installed as the governing power in Iraq with Ahmed Hassan al-Bakr as the new Iraqi President.
King Mohammed Zahir Shah of Afghanistan, while having surgery in Italy, is deposed by his cousin Mohammed Daoud Khan.
Apollo–Soyuz Test Project: An American Apollo and a Soviet Soyuz spacecraft dock with each other in orbit marking the first such link-up between spacecraft from the two nations.
East Timor is annexed and becomes the 27th province of Indonesia.

The opening of the Summer Olympics in Montreal is marred by 25 African teams boycotting the games because of New Zealand's participation. Contrary to rulings by other international sports organizations, the IOC had declined to exclude New Zealand because of their participation in South African sporting events during apartheid.
A structural failure leads to the collapse of a walkway at the Hyatt Regency in Kansas City, Missouri, killing 114 people and injuring more than 200.

main.desc: 1981 structural collapse in Kansas City, Missouri

events.text: The Manchester Metrolink, the first modern street-running light-rail system in the United Kingdom, was officially opened.

main.desc: Tram system in Greater Manchester, England

events.text: Brazil won the FIFA World Cup final against Italy 3–2 on penalties, following a 0–0 draw after extra time.
Brazil win their fourth World Cup title, defeating Italy 3–2 on penalties.
TWA Flight 800 exploded in mid-air and crashed into the Atlantic Ocean near East Moriches, New York.

main.desc: 1996 aviation accident in the Atlantic Ocean

events.text: TWA Flight 800: Off the coast of Long Island, New York, a Paris-bound TWA Boeing 747 explodes, killing all 230 on board.

main.desc: 1996 aviation accident in the Atlantic Ocean

events.text: After takeoff from Husein Sastranegara International Airport, Sempati Air Flight 304 crashes into a residential neighborhood in Bandung, killing 28 people.

main.desc: Airport in Bandung, West Java, Indonesia

events.text: The 7.0 Mw Papua New Guinea earthquake triggers a tsunami that destroys ten villages in Papua New Guinea, killing up to 2,700 people, and leaving several thousand injured.

main.desc: Severe earthquake and tsunami near Papua New Guinea

events.text: A diplomatic conference adopts the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court, establishing the permanent international court in The Hague, to prosecute individuals for genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes, and the crime of aggression.

main.desc: 1998 international treaty establishing the International Criminal Court

events.text: During approach to Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Airport, Alliance Air Flight 7412 suddenly crashes into a residential neighborhood in Patna, India, killing 60 people.
The 7.7 Mw Pangandaran tsunami earthquake severely affects the Indonesian island of Java, killing 668 people, and leaving more than 9,000 injured.

main.desc: Destructive tsunami earthquake south of Java Island

events.text: TAM Airlines Flight 3054 overran the runway at Congonhas Airport in São Paulo, Brazil, killing 199 people.
TAM Airlines Flight 3054, an Airbus A320, crashes into a warehouse after landing too fast and missing the end of the São Paulo–Congonhas Airport runway, killing 199 people.
Malaysia Airlines Flight 17 was shot down over eastern Ukraine, killing all 298 people on board.
Malaysia Airlines Flight 17, a Boeing 777, crashes near the border of Ukraine and Russia after being shot down. All 298 people on board are killed.
A French regional train on the Pau-Bayonne line crashes into a high-speed train near the town of Denguin, resulting in at least 25 injuries.
Eric Garner is killed by police officer Daniel Pantaleo in New York City, after the latter put him in a prohibited chokehold while arresting him.

main.desc: 2014 police killing of a black man in New York City

events.text: At least 120 people are killed and 130 injured by a suicide bombing in Diyala Governorate, Iraq.

main.desc: Terrorist suicide bombing in Diyala, Iraq

events.text: Battle of the Cremera as part of the Roman–Etruscan Wars. Veii ambushes and defeats the Roman army.

main.desc: Part of the Roman–Etruscan Wars (477 BC)

events.text: Roman–Persian Wars: Emperor Julian arrives at Antioch with a Roman expeditionary force (60,000 men) and stays there for nine months to launch a campaign against the Persian Empire.
Sack of Aquileia: After an earlier defeat on the Catalaunian Plains, Attila lays siege to the metropolis of Aquileia and eventually destroys it.

main.desc: Destruction of the Roman city by the Huns (452)

events.text: Chinese forces under general Li Shiji besiege the strategic fortress city of Anshi (Liaoning) during the Goguryeo–Tang War.
Battle of Alarcos: Almohad forces defeat the Castilian army of Alfonso VIII and force its retreat to Toledo.
Election of pope Honorius III following the death of pope Innocent III two days prior.
King Edward I issued an edict to expel all Jews from England.

links.t: History of the Jews in England

events.text: King Edward I of England issues the Edict of Expulsion, banishing all Jews (numbering about 16,000) from England.
The bishop of Florence blesses the first foundation stone for the new campanile (bell tower) of the Florence Cathedral, designed by the artist Giotto di Bondone.
France and England agree to the Truce of Leulinghem, inaugurating a 13-year peace, the longest period of sustained peace during the Hundred Years' War.
In Brussels, Prince Charles I is crowned Duke of Burgundy and Count of Flanders, a year after inheriting the title.

main.desc: Federal region of Belgium including the capital

events.text: The College of Arms is reincorporated by Royal charter signed by Queen Mary I of England and King Philip II of Spain.

main.desc: Corporation responsible for heraldry in England and Wales

events.text: Johann Sebastian Bach directed the first performance of his cantata Erforsche mich, Gott, und erfahre mein Herz in Leipzig.

links.t: Erforsche mich, Gott, und erfahre mein Herz, BWV 136

events.text: Johann Sebastian Bach leads the first performance of his cantata Erforsche mich, Gott, und erfahre mein Herz, BWV 136, in Leipzig on the eighth Sunday after Trinity.

links.t: Erforsche mich, Gott, und erfahre mein Herz, BWV 136

events.text: An explosion at a gunpowder magazine in Birgu, Malta, killed an estimated 200 people.

main.desc: Munitions depot accident in British Malta

events.text: A gunpowder magazine explosion in Birgu, Malta, kills around 200 people.

main.desc: Munitions depot accident in British Malta

events.text: The Treaties of Orebro end both the Anglo-Russian and Anglo-Swedish Wars.

main.desc: 1812 peace treaty between the UK, Sweden, and the Russian Empire

events.text: Pedro II, the last emperor of Brazil, was crowned at the Old Cathedral of Rio de Janeiro.

links.t: Coronation of the Emperor of Brazil
Old Cathedral of Rio de Janeiro

events.text: Coronation of Emperor Pedro II of Brazil.
Louis Faidherbe, French governor of Senegal, arrives to relieve French forces at Kayes, effectively ending El Hajj Umar Tall's war against the French.

links.t: List of colonial governors of Senegal

events.text: First ascent of Dent Blanche, one of the highest summits in the Alps.

main.desc: Mountain in the Pennine Alps in Valais Canton, Switzerland

events.text: American Civil War: Led by Colonel Robert Gould Shaw, the 54th Massachusetts Infantry Regiment, one of the first African-American military units in the Union Army, spearheaded an assault (pictured) on Fort Wagner, South Carolina.

American Civil War: Second Battle of Fort Wagner: One of the first formal African American military units, the 54th Massachusetts Volunteer Infantry, supported by several white regiments, attempts an unsuccessful assault on Confederate-held Battery Wagner.
The First Vatican Council decrees the dogma of papal infallibility.
The Ballot Act 1872 in the United Kingdom introduced the requirement that parliamentary and local government elections be held by secret ballot.

main.desc: United Kingdom law reforming the electoral system

events.text: Newsboys from Long Island City turned over a distribution wagon for the New York Journal, marking the start of the Newsboys' strike of 1899.
The U.S. Congress forms the Aviation Section, U.S. Signal Corps, giving official status to aircraft within the U.S. Army for the first time.

main.desc: Bicameral legislature of the United States

events.text: Adolf Hitler publishes Mein Kampf.
Nationalist rebels attempted a coup against the Second Spanish Republic, sparking the Spanish Civil War.

main.desc: Major faction in the Spanish Civil War of 1936 to 1939

events.text: World War II: During the Beisfjord massacre in Norway, 15 Norwegian paramilitary guards help members of the SS to kill 288 political prisoners from Yugoslavia.
The Germans test fly the Messerschmitt Me 262 using its jet engines for the first time.
World War II: Hideki Tōjō resigns as Prime Minister of Japan because of numerous setbacks in the war effort.

main.desc: Japanese general, prime minister from 1941 to 1944

events.text: Francisco Javier Arana, the chief of the Guatemalan armed forces, was killed in a shootout with supporters of President Juan José Arévalo.
Angered by racism and poverty, African American residents of the Hough neighborhood of Cleveland began to riot for six days.
Human spaceflight: Gemini 10 is launched from Cape Kennedy on a 70-hour mission that includes docking with an orbiting Agena target vehicle.

main.desc: Spaceflight with a crew or passengers

events.text: A racially charged incident in a bar sparks the six-day Hough riots in Cleveland, Ohio; 1,700 Ohio National Guard troops intervene to restore order.

main.desc: Civil unrest and rioting in Cleveland, Ohio in 1966

events.text: Intel is founded in Mountain View, California.
An Antonov An-22 of the Soviet Air Forces crashes into the Atlantic Ocean, killing all 23 aboard.
At the Olympic Games in Montreal, Nadia Comăneci (pictured) became the first gymnast to score a perfect 10 for her routine on the uneven bars.

links.t: Gymnastics at the 1976 Summer Olympics – Women's uneven bars

events.text: Nadia Comăneci becomes the first person in Olympic Games history to score a perfect 10 in gymnastics at the 1976 Summer Olympics.
A landslide occurs on the Iliwerung volcano in Indonesia, triggering a tsunami that kills over 530 and leaves 700 missing.
A Canadair CL-44 and Sukhoi Su-15 collide in mid-air near Yerevan, Armenia, killing four.
Two hundred sixty-eight Guatemalan campesinos ("peasants" or "country people") are slain in the Plan de Sánchez massacre.
Parts of the dismembered body of Swedish prostitute Catrine da Costa were found in Stockholm.
A gunman massacred 21 people and injured 15 others at a McDonald's restaurant in the district of San Ysidro of San Diego, California.
McDonald's massacre in San Ysidro, California: James Oliver Huberty kills 21 people and injures 19 others before being shot dead by police.
American actress Rebecca Schaeffer was shot and killed by Robert John Bardo, eventually prompting the passage of anti-stalking laws in California.
A picture of Les Horribles Cernettes was taken, which became the first ever photo posted to the World Wide Web.
The bombing of the Asociación Mutual Israelita Argentina (Argentine Jewish Community Center) in Buenos Aires kills 85 people (mostly Jewish) and injures 300.

main.desc: 1994 attack on a Jewish Community Centre in Buenos Aires, Argentina

events.text: Rwandan genocide: The Rwandan Patriotic Front takes control of Gisenyi and north western Rwanda, forcing the interim government into Zaire and ending the genocide.
Selena's album Dreaming of You, instrumental in popularizing Tejano music, was posthumously released.
On the Caribbean island of Montserrat, the Soufrière Hills volcano erupts. Over the course of several years, it devastates the island, destroying the capital, forcing most of the population to flee.

main.desc: British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean

events.text: Storms provoke severe flooding on the Saguenay River, beginning one of Quebec's costliest natural disasters ever.

main.desc: 1996 flash flood that hit Saguenay-Lac-Saint-Jean region of Quebec, Canada

events.text: Battle of Mullaitivu: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam capture the Sri Lanka Army's base, killing over 1,200 soldiers.

main.desc: Part of the Sri Lankan Civil War

events.text: A Consolidated PB4Y-2 Privateer crashes near Estes Park, Colorado, killing both crew members.

main.desc: Patrol bomber of the US Navy, 1943

events.text: A suicide bomber attacked an Israeli tour bus at Burgas Airport, Bulgaria, resulting in the military branch of Hezbollah being designated a terrorist organization by the European Union.

main.desc: Suicide attack against Israeli civilians at the Burgas Airport in Bulgaria

events.text: At least seven people are killed and 32 others are injured after a bomb explodes on an Israeli tour bus at Burgas Airport, Bulgaria.

main.desc: Suicide attack against Israeli civilians at the Burgas Airport in Bulgaria

events.text: The Government of Detroit, with up to $20 billion in debt, files for the largest municipal bankruptcy in U.S. history.
The conviction of former Italian prime minister Silvio Berlusconi, who had been found guilty of paying for an underage prostitute, was overturned on appeal.
The Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant requires Christians to either accept dhimmi status, emigrate from ISIL lands, or be killed.
An arson attack at the studio of Kyoto Animation in Japan led to the deaths of 36 people.
A man sets fire to an anime studio in Fushimi-ku, Kyoto, Japan, killing 36 people and injuring dozens of others.
The Great Fire of Rome causes widespread devastation and rages on for six days, destroying half of the city.
Leontius, Roman usurper, is crowned Eastern emperor at Tarsus (modern Turkey). He is recognized in Antioch and makes it his capital.
Umayyad conquest of Hispania: Battle of Guadalete: Umayyad forces under Tariq ibn Ziyad defeat the Visigoths led by King Roderic.

links.t: Muslim conquest of the Iberian Peninsula

events.text: Bardanes Tourkos is proclaimed emperor by rebellious Byzantine troops.
Battle of Simancas: King Ramiro II of León defeats the Moorish army under Caliph Abd-al-Rahman III near the city of Simancas.

main.desc: Battle of the Reconquista in 939 AD

events.text: Arab–Byzantine wars: After initial Byzantine gains at the Battle of Apamea, a lone Kurdish rider killed Byzantine commander Damian Dalassenos, allowing Fatimid troops to turn the tide of the battle.

main.desc: Series of wars between the 7th and 11th centuries

events.text: Arab–Byzantine wars: Battle of Apamea: Fatimids defeat a Byzantine army near Apamea.

main.desc: Series of wars between the 7th and 11th centuries

events.text: Second War of Scottish Independence: Scottish forces under Sir Archibald Douglas were heavily defeated by the English at the Battle of Halidon Hill while trying to relieve Berwick-upon-Tweed.
Wars of Scottish Independence: The English win a decisive victory over the Scots in the battle of Halidon Hill.

main.desc: War of national liberation between Scotland and England

events.text: Italian War of 1542–46: The first Siege of Boulogne begins.

main.desc: Ninth phase of the Italian Wars

events.text: The English warship Mary Rose sank outside Portsmouth during the Battle of the Solent; it was raised from the seabed in 1982.
The Tudor warship Mary Rose sinks off Portsmouth; in 1982 the wreck is salvaged in one of the most complex and expensive projects in the history of maritime archaeology.

main.desc: Period of English history (1485–1603) under the Tudor dynasty

events.text: Mary I was proclaimed Queen of England, deposing Lady Jane Grey after nine days of de facto rule.

main.desc: Queen of England and Ireland from 1553 to 1558

events.text: The attempt to install Lady Jane Grey as Queen of England collapses after only nine days.

main.desc: Disputed Queen of England and Ireland in 1553

events.text: Anglo-Spanish War: Battle of Gravelines: The Spanish Armada is sighted in the English Channel.

main.desc: War between the kingdoms of Spain and England

events.text: Representatives of the Iroquois Confederacy sign the Nanfan Treaty, ceding a large territory north of the Ohio River to England.
Great Northern War: Polish–Saxon forces were defeated by a Swedish army half their size at the Battle of Kliszów.

Great Northern War: A numerically superior Polish-Saxon army of Augustus II the Strong, operating from an advantageous defensive position, is defeated by a Swedish army half its size under the command of King Charles XII in the Battle of Klissow.
The Ottoman army defeats the Iranian army under Nader Shah in the battle of Baghdad.
Georg Anton Schäffer was forced to depart for China after his unsuccessful attempt to seize the Hawaiian Kingdom for the Russian Empire.
Unsuccessful in his attempt to conquer the Kingdom of Hawaiʻi for the Russian-American Company, Georg Anton Schäffer is forced to admit defeat and leave Kauaʻi.

main.desc: Attempt to claim the Hawaiian Kingdom for the Russian Empire (1815–17)

events.text: Coronation of George IV of the United Kingdom.

main.desc: King of the United Kingdom from 1820 to 1830

events.text: The British Medical Association is founded as the Provincial Medical and Surgical Association by Sir Charles Hastings at a meeting in the Board Room of the Worcester Infirmary.
SS Great Britain, the first ocean-going ship with both an iron hull and a screw propeller, was launched (pictured) in Bristol, England.
Brunel's steamship the SS Great Britain is launched, becoming the first ocean-going craft with an iron hull and screw propeller, becoming the largest vessel afloat in the world.
A fire in Manhattan, New York City, destroyed 345 buildings, killed 30 people, and caused at least $5 million in damage.

main.t: Great New York City Fire of 1845

events.text: Great New York City Fire of 1845: The last great fire to affect Manhattan begins early in the morning and is subdued that afternoon. The fire kills four firefighters and 26 civilians and destroys 345 buildings.

main.t: Great New York City Fire of 1845

events.text: The two-day Seneca Falls Convention, the first women's-rights and feminist convention held in the United States, opened in Seneca Falls, New York.
Women's rights: A two-day Women's Rights Convention opens in Seneca Falls, New York.

main.desc: Rights claimed for women and girls worldwide

events.text: American Civil War: Morgan's Raid: At Buffington Island in Ohio, Confederate General John Hunt Morgan's raid into the north is mostly thwarted when a large group of his men are captured while trying to escape across the Ohio River.
Taiping Rebellion: Third Battle of Nanking: The Qing dynasty finally defeats the Taiping Heavenly Kingdom.
Franco-Prussian War: France declares war on Prussia.
The first line of the Paris Metro opens for operation.

main.desc: Oldest rapid transit line of Paris, France

events.text: French cyclist Maurice Garin won the first edition of the Tour de France.
Maurice Garin wins the first Tour de France.
First World War: The "worst 24 hours in Australia's entire history" occurred when Australian forces unsuccessfully attacked German defences at Fromelles, France.
World War I: Battle of Fromelles: British and Australian troops attack German trenches as part of the Battle of the Somme.
Following Peace Day celebrations marking the end of the First World War, English ex-servicemen unhappy with unemployment and other grievances rioted and burned down Luton Town Hall.
The rigid airship USS Macon surprises the USS Houston near Clipperton Island with a mail delivery for President Franklin D. Roosevelt, demonstrating its potential for tracking ships at sea.
The July 1936 military uprising in Barcelona begins.
Spanish Civil War: The CNT and UGT call a general strike in Spain – mobilizing workers' militias against the Nationalist forces. People's Olympiad of Barcelona cancelled.
World War II: Battle of Cape Spada: The Royal Navy and the Regia Marina clash; the Italian light cruiser Bartolomeo Colleoni sinks, with 121 casualties.
Field Marshal Ceremony: First occasion in World War II that Adolf Hitler appoints field marshals due to military achievements.
World War II: Army order 112 forms the Intelligence Corps of the British Army.

main.desc: Intelligence arm of the British Army

events.text: World War II: The Second Happy Time of Hitler's submarines comes to an end, as the increasingly effective American convoy system compels them to return to the central Atlantic.

main.desc: Period of German sinking of merchant ships off the East Coast during the Second World War

events.text: World War II: Rome is heavily bombed by more than 500 Allied aircraft, inflicting thousands of casualties.

main.t: Bombing of Rome in World War II

events.text: Prime Minister of the shadow Burmese government, Bogyoke Aung San and eight others are assassinated.
Korean politician Lyuh Woon-hyung is assassinated.
Opening of the Summer Olympics in Helsinki, Finland.
The Ordeal of Gilbert Pinfold, a largely autobiographical novel by Evelyn Waugh, was published.
The largely autobiographical novel The Ordeal of Gilbert Pinfold by Evelyn Waugh is published.
Tunisia imposes a blockade on the French naval base at Bizerte; the French would capture the entire town four days later.

Joe Walker flies a North American X-15 to a record altitude of 106,010 meters (347,800 feet) on X-15 Flight 90. Exceeding an altitude of 100 km, this flight qualifies as a human spaceflight under international convention.
Vietnam War: At a rally in Saigon, South Vietnamese Prime Minister Nguyễn Khánh calls for expanding the war into North Vietnam.

Piedmont Airlines Flight 22, a Piedmont Airlines Boeing 727-22, and a twin-engine Cessna 310 collide over Hendersonville, North Carolina, USA. Both aircraft are destroyed and all passengers and crew are killed, including John T. McNaughton, an advisor to Robert McNamara.
Chappaquiddick incident: U.S. Senator Ted Kennedy crashes his car into a tidal pond at Chappaquiddick Island, Massachusetts, killing his passenger Mary Jo Kopechne.

main.desc: 1969 car accident and drowning in Massachusetts

events.text: Dhofar Rebellion: British SAS units help the Omani government against Popular Front for the Liberation of Oman rebels in the Battle of Mirbat.

links.t: Popular Front for the Liberation of Oman

events.text: Environmental activists bombed the port facilities in Bunbury, Western Australia, in an attempt to disrupt the woodchipping industry.
Sagarmatha National Park in Nepal is created.

The world's first Global Positioning System (GPS) signal is transmitted from Navigation Technology Satellite 2 (NTS-2) and received at Rockwell Collins in Cedar Rapids, Iowa, at 12:41 a.m. Eastern time (ET).
The Sandinista rebels overthrow the government of the Somoza family in Nicaragua.

main.desc: Nicaraguan socialist political party founded in 1961

events.text: The oil tanker SS Atlantic Empress collides with another oil tanker, causing the largest ever ship-borne oil spill.

main.desc: Greek oil tanker; collided, sank, and spilled oil in the Caribbean Sea in 1979

events.text: Opening of the Summer Olympics in Moscow.

main.desc: Multi-sport event in Moscow, Russian SFSR, Soviet Union

events.text: In a private meeting with U.S. President Ronald Reagan, French President François Mitterrand reveals the existence of the Farewell Dossier, a collection of documents showing the Soviet Union had been stealing American technological research and development.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1981 to 1989

events.text: In one of the first militant attacks by Hezbollah, David S. Dodge, president of the American University of Beirut, is kidnapped.

main.desc: Islamist movement and militant group based in Lebanon

events.text: The first three-dimensional reconstruction of a human head in a CT is published.
The Val di Stava dam collapses, killing 268 people in Val di Stava, Italy.

main.desc: 1985 dam structural failure near Tesero, Italy

events.text: United Airlines Flight 232 crashes in Sioux City, Iowa, killing 111.
A car bomb killed the anti-Mafia judge Paolo Borsellino and five policemen in Palermo, Italy, less than two months after the murder of Borsellino's friend and colleague Giovanni Falcone.
A car bomb kills Judge Paolo Borsellino and five members of his escort.
Alas Chiricanas Flight 00901 is destroyed by a bomb after takeoff from Enrique Adolfo Jiménez Airport in Colón, Panama, killing 21.
The Troubles: The Provisional Irish Republican Army announced that it would resume its ceasefire, ending its 28-year campaign against British rule in Northern Ireland.
The Troubles: The Provisional Irish Republican Army resumes a ceasefire to end their 25-year paramilitary campaign to end British rule in Northern Ireland.
Guinean President Alpha Condé survives an attempted assassination and coup d'état at his residence in Conakry.
Syrian civil war: The People's Protection Units (YPG) capture the city of Kobanî without resistance, starting the Rojava conflict in Northeast Syria.
The NASA spacecraft Cassini took a photograph of Saturn with Earth in the distance (detail pictured), for which people were invited to "wave at Saturn".
Gunmen ambushed an Egyptian military checkpoint in the Libyan Desert near Farafra, killing 22 soldiers.

main.desc: Terror attack in Egypt's New Valley Governorate

events.text: Gunmen in Egypt's western desert province of New Valley Governorate attack a military checkpoint, killing at least 21 soldiers. Egypt reportedly declares a state of emergency on its border with Sudan.
The Knesset passes the controversial Nationality Bill, which defines the State of Israel as the nation-state of the Jewish people.

links.t: Basic Law: Israel as the Nation-State of the Jewish People

events.text: Neary's, a New York City Irish pub popular with political elites, closed.

main.desc: Irish pub in New York City, 1967 to 2024

events.text: Siege of Jerusalem: Titus, son of emperor Vespasian, storms the Fortress of Antonia north of the Temple Mount. The Roman army is drawn into street fights with the Zealots.
Consecration of pope Hormisdas following the death of pope Symmachus the previous day.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 514 to 523

events.text: Kardam of Bulgaria defeats Byzantine Emperor Constantine VI at the Battle of Marcellae.
Rollo lays siege to Chartres.
Richard I of England officially invested as Duke of Normandy.
Treaty of San Germano is signed at San Germano between Holy Roman Emperor Frederick II and Pope Gregory IX. A Dominican named Guala is responsible for the negotiations.

main.desc: 1230 treaty between the Holy Roman Empire and the papacy

events.text: Second War of Scottish Inde­pen­dence: The Scottish-held town of Berwick-upon-Tweed surrendered to English forces, ending a siege led by King Edward III.

The Battle of Kellistown was fought on this day between the forces of the English led by Roger Mortimer, 4th Earl of March against the O'Byrnes and O'Tooles under the command of Art Óg mac Murchadha Caomhánach, the most powerful Chieftain in Leinster.
During the first Japanese invasion of Korea, Japanese forces led by Toyotomi Hideyoshi captured Pyongyang, although they were ultimately unable to hold it.
Wars of the Three Kingdoms: After crossing the Firth of Forth, English Commonwealth forces defeated a Scottish army at the Battle of Inverkeithing, opening the rest of the country to occupation.
A fire in Oulu, Finland almost completely destroyed the fourth district, which covered the southern part of the city and was by far the largest of the city districts.

Seventh Ottoman–Venetian War: The Ottoman Empire captures Nauplia, the capital of the Republic of Venice's "Kingdom of the Morea", thereby opening the way to the swift Ottoman reconquest of the Morea.
Canadian explorer Pierre Gaultier de Varennes et de La Vérendrye reaches the western shore of Lake Michigan.

main.t: Pierre Gaultier de Varennes, sieur de La Vérendrye
main.desc: 18th-century French Canadian military officer, fur trader and explorer

events.text: Scottish explorer Alexander Mackenzie reached the Pacific coast at Bella Coola, British Columbia, completing the first recorded transcontinental crossing of North America north of Mexico.
Tekle Giyorgis I begins his first of six reigns as Emperor of Ethiopia.

main.desc: Emperor of Ethiopia intermittently between 1779 and 1800

events.text: French brothers Claude and Nicéphore Niépce received a patent for their Pyréolophore, one of the world's first internal combustion engines.
Nicéphore Niépce is awarded a patent by Napoleon for the Pyréolophore, the world's first internal combustion engine, after it successfully powered a boat upstream on the river Saône in France.
Citizens of Bogotá, New Granada declare independence from Spain.

main.desc: Capital and largest city of Colombia

events.text: Seneca and Shawnee people agree to relinquish their land in western Ohio for 60,000 acres west of the Mississippi River.

main.desc: Haudenosaunee group of the Eastern Woodlands of North America

events.text: The first Women's Rights Convention in Seneca Falls, New York, a two-day event, concludes.
American Civil War: Battle of Peachtree Creek: Near Atlanta, Georgia, Confederate forces led by General John Bell Hood unsuccessfully attack Union troops under General William T. Sherman.

main.desc: 1864 battle of the American Civil War

events.text: Austro-Prussian War: Battle of Lissa: The Austrian Navy, led by Admiral Wilhelm von Tegetthoff, defeats the Italian Navy near the island of Vis in the Adriatic Sea.
The United States Congress established the Indian Peace Commission to seek peace treaties with a number of Native American tribes.

main.desc: Bicameral legislature of the United States

links.t: Native Americans in the United States

events.text: British Columbia joins the Canadian Confederation.
The Football Association legalizes professionalism in association football under pressure from the British Football Association.

main.desc: Governing body of association football in England

events.text: The Ford Motor Company ships its first automobile.
In Finland, a new electoral law is ratified, guaranteeing the country the first and equal right to vote in the world. Finnish women are the first in Europe to receive the right to vote.
George V reviewed more than 200 Royal Navy vessels at Spithead, England.

main.desc: King of the United Kingdom from 1910 to 1936

events.text: Serbian prime minister Nikola Pašić and Yugoslav Committee president Ante Trumbić signed the Corfu Declaration, agreeing to seek the establishment of the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes.
World War I: The Corfu Declaration, which leads to the creation of the post-war Kingdom of Yugoslavia, is signed by the Yugoslav Committee and Kingdom of Serbia.
The Greek Army takes control of Silivri after Greece is awarded the city by the Paris Peace Conference; by 1923 Greece effectively lost control to the Turks.

main.desc: District and municipality in Istanbul, Turkey

events.text: The League of Nations awards mandates of Togoland to France and Tanganyika to the United Kingdom.
In the Preußenschlag, German President Hindenburg places Prussia directly under the rule of the national government.

main.desc: Takeover by German chancellor von Papen

events.text: Labor unrest in the U.S.: Police in Minneapolis fire upon striking truck drivers, during the Minneapolis Teamsters Strike of 1934, killing two and wounding sixty-seven.
West Coast waterfront strike: In Seattle, police fire tear gas on and club 2,000 striking longshoremen. The governor of Oregon calls out the National Guard to break a strike on the Portland docks.

main.desc: Labor strike by longshoremen in California, Oregon, and Washington

events.text: Switzerland: A Royal Dutch Airlines plane en route from Milan to Frankfurt crashes into a Swiss mountain, killing thirteen.
The July 1936 military uprising in Barcelona is defeated by anarchist militias and Republican loyalists, beginning the Spanish Revolution of 1936.
The Montreux Convention is signed in Switzerland, authorizing Turkey to fortify the Dardanelles and Bosphorus but guaranteeing free passage to ships of all nations in peacetime.

main.t: Montreux Convention Regarding the Regime of the Straits
main.desc: 1936 treaty governing the Bosporus and Dardanelles straits

events.text: The United States Department of Justice files suit in New York City against the motion picture industry charging violations of the Sherman Antitrust Act in regards to the studio system.  The case would eventually result in a break-up of the industry in 1948.
Denmark leaves the League of Nations.
California opens its first freeway, the Arroyo Seco Parkway.
Soviet leader Joseph Stalin consolidates the Commissariats of Home Affairs and National Security to form the NKVD and names Lavrentiy Beria its chief.
World War II: Adolf Hitler survives an assassination attempt led by German Army Colonel Claus von Stauffenberg.
The Israel–Syria Mixed Armistice Commission brokers the last of four ceasefire agreements to end the 1948 Arab–Israeli War.

main.desc: Commission overseeing Israeli–Syrian ceasefire after the 1948 Arab-Israeli war

events.text: Korean War: After a month-long campaign, much of the North Korean air force was destroyed by United Nations forces.
Cold War: In Philadelphia, Harry Gold pleads guilty to spying for the Soviet Union by passing secrets from atomic scientist Klaus Fuchs.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: After a month-long campaign, the majority of North Korea's Air Force was destroyed by anti-communist forces.

main.desc: Air warfare branch of North Korea's military

events.text: Abdullah I of Jordan was assassinated while visiting the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem.

links.t: Assassination of Abdullah I of Jordan

events.text: King Abdullah I of Jordan is assassinated by a Palestinian while attending Friday prayers in Jerusalem.

links.t: Assassination of Abdullah I of Jordan

events.text: Germany: Otto John, head of West Germany's secret service, defects to East Germany.
The Polaris missile is successfully launched from a submarine, the USS George Washington, for the first time.
French military forces break the Tunisian siege of Bizerte.
Vietnam War: Viet Cong forces attack the capital of Định Tường Province, Cái Bè, killing 11 South Vietnamese military personnel and 40 civilians (30 of whom are children).
The first games of the Special Olympics (athletes pictured), for athletes with intellectual disabilities, were held at Soldier Field in Chicago.

main.desc: Multi-sport event in Chicago, Illinois, US

events.text: The first International Special Olympics Summer Games are held at Soldier Field in Chicago, with about 1,000 athletes with intellectual disabilities.
The Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle landed on the Sea of Tranquillity, where Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first men to walk on the Moon six and a half hours later (bootprint pictured).

Apollo program: Apollo 11's crew successfully makes the first human landing on the Moon in the Sea of Tranquility. Americans Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin become the first humans to walk on the Moon six and a half hours later.
A cease fire is announced between Honduras and El Salvador, six days after the beginning of the "Football War".
Turkish invasion of Cyprus: Forces from Turkey invade Cyprus after a coup d'état, organized by the dictator of Greece, against president Makarios.
The Viking 1 lander became the first spacecraft to successfully land on Mars and perform its mission.
The American Viking 1 lander successfully lands on Mars.
Rain from a stalled thunderstorm caused six dams to fail, flooding Johnstown, Pennsylvania, resulting in 84 deaths and $340 in damages.
The Central Intelligence Agency releases documents under the Freedom of Information Act revealing it had engaged in mind-control experiments.

main.desc: U.S. intelligence and covert action agency

events.text: The Johnstown flood of 1977 kills 84 people and causes millions of dollars in damages.
Aeroflot Flight B-2 crashes after takeoff from Vitim Airport in the Sakha Republic, killing 39.
Somali Airlines Flight 40 crashes in Balad, Somalia, killing 50 people.
